commentaire:
(a) Time left until the outcome is known
- About 10 days (from 17 Nov 2026 to the cutoff at 16:00 UTC on 27 Nov 2026 / 00:00 MYT on 28 Nov 2026). The key announcements are widely expected in the final week before nomination day.

(b) Status quo outcome if nothing changed
- As of mid-November no GPS candidate has been publicly named for Bawang Assan. SUPP has publicly put forward Kevin Lau and has submitted lists to the Premier, while PDP has pressed an incumbency claim (Wong Soon Koh joined PDP) and submitted names including Joshua Ting. The final decision rests with GPS chair Abang Johari and historically GPS has released its full line-up very close to nomination day. If nothing else changes, the most likely immediate outcome is that GPS will make a single public naming for Bawang Assan in the pre-nomination batch (i.e., a candidate will be announced before the cutoff).

(c) Scenario that results in an unexpected outcome
- GPS fails to make any public announcement naming its Bawang Assan candidate before the cutoff because of an internal breakdown in talks (e.g., a last-minute veto from a component leader, an unresolved candidate eligibility/health/legal issue, or a deliberate strategic delay). Alternatively, Abang Johari could break expectations and award the seat to a candidate from a different GPS component (PBB/PRS) or to someone not currently identified as SUPP/PDP — for example if GPS prioritises a specially chosen unity candidate, or if the incumbent withdraws and GPS parachutes in a different component member as a compromise.

Rationale and probabilities
- Baseline / status-quo weighting: most institutional coalitions try to resolve seat disputes before nomination day, and GPS has precedent of announcing the full lineup very close to the cutoff. That makes “no announcement” less likely but still possible if talks collapse.
- Candidate-party weighting:
  - PDP has a strong claim via incumbency (Wong Soon Koh joined PDP after PSB dissolved), and PDP has reportedly submitted names. Incumbency and the desire to keep senior figures within their component intact mean PDP has a meaningful advantage.
  - SUPP has a strong local/legacy claim in Sibu and has publicly pushed Kevin Lau and submitted lists, which signals active contestation and real chances of SUPP being awarded the seat.
  - PBB/PRS or a non-SUPP/PDP candidate is possible but less likely: this would be a notable compromise move and would risk intra-coalition friction; it is plausible only if GPS leadership wants to avoid direct loss of face for either SUPP or PDP.
  - “No GPS candidate named before cutoff” is possible if negotiations truly break down or a late procedural/health/legal issue prevents a naming, but GPS has strong incentives to avoid leaving a seat unresolved going into nomination.

Given the above, I put moderate weight on the incumbency/PDP claim, meaningful weight on SUPP’s visible push, and a small residual for unexpected compromise or a failure to announce.

Final probabilities
SUPP: 30%
PDP: 50%
PBB or PRS (or a candidate who is not a member of SUPP or PDP): 5%
No GPS candidate for Bawang Assan publicly named before the cutoff: 15%
